generated: measured from docs/art/rigs/iso-rig-pack/wharf-kit-iso/wharfIsoRig.js in a standalone V8 host at rig-default dimensions, tide and clearance (tideRange 4.4, clearance 0.8 — Hillsborough Bay). The cell is PARAMETRIC: these numbers hold for a bake at the rig's defaults and for no other, so re-measure rather than trusting them after any authoring change. 17 -> 19 keys: gangway and floatPiles are new, and timberFloat MOVED (300x348 -> 199x195) because its guide piles, mooring chain and seabed block left it for floatPiles — one sprite could not hold a raft that rides and furniture that is driven into the seabed, and the rig had always tagged exactly those `fixed`.

projection.pivot: projection of the model origin (footprint centre at chart datum) — the rig reports px,py per bake
projection.cellRule: pivot-aligned union of the rig's RETURNED BUFFER extents across EVERY CELL THE KEY BAKES — all 8 facings, and for gangway all 8 x 9 rungs too — floor/ceil, pivot-inclusive: cellW=ceil(max(w-1-px))-floor(min(-px))+1, pivotX=-floor(min(-px)), likewise Y. Measure the BUFFER, not the ink bbox — ink gives floatSet 751x556 against the 757x592 recorded here, and every one of the 19 keys then disagrees. Unioning a rung axis is what makes the ladder swappable: gangway's 9 rungs measure 296..403 px tall on their own and share one 404 px cell at one pivot, so the runtime changes sprite without moving the object.

azimuth.measured: -46.75 deg of screen rotation per dir step, identical to houseIsoRig / wharfBuildingRig / interiorIsoRig (all registered CounterClockwise)

tide.note: tide is continuous in the rig and NOT a baked state axis; one water level is baked and the wet mask carries the rest

deck.note: deckZ = tideRange + clearance, the height a FIXED family's deck stands at and therefore the height of the drawn quay face. Presets that pin deckZ themselves (lowPier, tallPier, sheetCell) ignore it — which is exactly why those three cells did not move. The same clearance sets a float's gangway abutment, so a ramp meets the deck rather than stepping above it.

worstSheetByMaxDim.note: A texture cap binds on the LONGEST SIDE, not on area — size import headroom off THIS, not off worstSheet (which is the worst by area). Cells are parametric, so re-measure rather than trusting either field after an authoring change. The gangway's 9-rung sheet is the worst by AREA and does NOT take this field: 3636 px is still inside sheetedPier's 3784, so the family's binding side is unchanged — but its own headroom is 460 px and a rung is 404 of them, so the ladder cannot be lengthened without re-packing.

cells.note: The raft AND its sliding hoops. A guide hoop is bolted to the raft and slides up the pile as the tide takes her, so it rides; only the pile itself stands. The rig's `fixed` tag could not make that split on its own - it answers whether a thing ROCKS with the raft, and a hoop on a pile does not rock and does ride.

299 px, one narrower than before the hoops left the `fixed` set. A guide hoop is bolted to the RAFT, so it rocks with her; the rig had it exempt from the float's own rock transform along with the pile it slides on. Correcting that moves this cell, floatSet's and plasticSet's pixels by a fraction of a degree of pitch.

The other half of timberFloat: guide piles, mooring chain and seabed block. No raft, and NO HOOPS - the collars slide with the raft and are drawn there. It measures EXACTLY the cell timberFloat used to before the split (300x348, pivot 149,216), so the piles land where they were always drawn and only the raft moves.

THE ONLY KEY WITH A SECOND SHEET AXIS. A brow's hinge is bolted to fixed ground and its landing rides a float, so its picture is a function of the tide and not merely of its position: one cell can only ever be right at one water level, which is what #735 refused. 8 facings ACROSS, 9 rungs DOWN, cell index = rung*8 + facing. The drops are the rig's own gangwayDrops() at the baked defaults (clearance - freeboard = 0.40 m at highest water, tideRange + clearance - freeboard = 4.80 m at lowest, in 0.55 m steps); the cell is the union across all 72, so every rung shares one pivot and the runtime swaps sprite without moving the object. Baked at run 12 m — Nine Mile Creek's own gap between the apron face and the float run, because the drawn brow and the walkable one must be the same brow (ADR 0010).
